description: Track A Phase 1 — MicroBlaze + AXI4-Lite + GEMM Tier 1 benchmark on Arty A7-100T

userStories.title: Parameterize ternary_gemm DEPTH and replace explicit dot instantiations with a generate loop
userStories.description: As an RTL engineer, I need ternary_gemm to support arbitrary DEPTH so it can drive real BitNet layers (e.g. DEPTH=768 for a 768-wide embedding projection) without manually adding dot instances.
acceptanceCriteria: DEPTH parameter drives all array sizing in ternary_gemm.v — no hardcoded 4
Explicit dot_0..dot_3 instantiations replaced with a generate loop over COLS
Testbench tb_ternary_gemm.v updated to sweep DEPTH=4, DEPTH=16, DEPTH=64
make tb_ternary_gemm passes for all three DEPTH values
Python verify/verify_gemm_simple.py still passes
userStories.notes: Replaced explicit dot_0..dot_3 instantiations with generate loop. Testbench parameterized with DEPTH_VAL sweep (4/16/64). All tests + Python verify pass.

userStories.title: Create AXI4-Lite slave wrapper for ternary_gemm
userStories.description: As an RTL engineer, I need an AXI4-Lite slave that wraps ternary_gemm so MicroBlaze can drive it via memory-mapped registers without custom bus logic.
acceptanceCriteria: New file rtl/axi_gemm_wrapper.v implementing AXI4-Lite slave
Register map: 0x00=CTRL (bit0=start, bit1=rst), 0x04=ACTIVATION (int8), 0x08=WEIGHT_ENC[31:0], 0x0C=WEIGHT_ENC[63:32 for >16 cols], 0x10..0x1C=ACC_OUT[3:0] read-only
CTRL.done bit (bit31) set when valid_out pulses, cleared on next write to CTRL
AXI4-Lite read/write handshake (AWVALID/AWREADY/WVALID/WREADY/BVALID/BREADY/ARVALID/ARREADY/RVALID/RREADY) fully implemented
New testbench tb/tb_axi_gemm_wrapper.v with AXI4-Lite BFM verifies: write activation + weight, poll done, read acc_out matches expected
make tb_axi_gemm_wrapper passes
userStories.notes: Created axi_gemm_wrapper.v with full AXI4-Lite handshake (AW/W/B/AR/R), register map (CTRL/ACTIVATION/WEIGHT_ENC/ACC_OUT), valid_in pulse on ACTIVATION write, done flag on valid_out, CTRL write clears done. Testbench with AXI BFM verifies 4 rows x 3 DEPTHs (4/16/64). All 47 tests pass.

userStories.title: BRAM weight cache for 1M ternary parameters
userStories.description: As an RTL engineer, I need on-chip BRAM storage for packed 2-bit ternary weights so Tier 1 benchmarks can run without DDR3.
acceptanceCriteria: New file rtl/weight_bram.v: dual-port BRAM, write port AXI4-Lite accessible (MicroBlaze loads weights), read port drives weight_enc bus of axi_gemm_wrapper
Packing: 4 ternary weights per byte (2 bits each), 1M params = 250 KB = 34.7 BRAM36 tiles — confirm fits in Artix-7 remaining budget
BRAM address width parameterized (default covers 250 KB)
Testbench tb/tb_weight_bram.v: write 16 packed weights via AXI, read back via weight port, verify no corruption
make tb_weight_bram passes
userStories.notes: Created weight_bram.v with dual-port BRAM (AXI4-Lite write port + combinatorial weight_enc read port). Default ADDR_WIDTH=18 covers 256KB = 1M ternary params (4/byte). Testbench with AXI BFM verifies write, readback, byte strobes, non-zero addressing, and combinational weight port read. Tests pass for ADDR_WIDTH=4 and ADDR_WIDTH=8. All 8 test targets pass.

userStories.title: Vivado block design: MicroBlaze + AXI Interconnect + GEMM IP + UART
userStories.description: As an FPGA engineer, I need a Vivado block design that integrates MicroBlaze with the ternary GEMM accelerator IP so I can build a bitstream and run firmware.
acceptanceCriteria: axi_gemm_wrapper.v and weight_bram.v packaged as Vivado IP (ip/ directory with component.xml)

Block design (Arty7/arty7.bd or tcl/create_bd.tcl) includes: MicroBlaze (no FPU, no cache), AXI4-Lite Interconnect, GEMM IP at 0x44000000, Weight BRAM at 0x44010000, AXI UART16550 at 0x40600000, GPIO for LEDs at 0x40000000
generate_bitstream.tcl runs without errors in Vivado 2024.x batch mode
LUT utilization after implementation < 63,400 (100% of Artix-7 A100T)
Timing closure at 100 MHz (WNS >= 0)
userStories.notes: Created Vivado IP packaging scripts (ip/package_axi_gemm_wrapper.tcl, ip/package_weight_bram.tcl). Block design TCL (Arty7/create_bd.tcl) sets up MicroBlaze (no FPU/cache) + AXI4-Lite Interconnect + GEMM IP @ 0x44000000 + Weight BRAM @ 0x44010000 + AXI UART16550 @ 0x40600000 + GPIO LEDs @ 0x40000000. Bitstream generation script (Arty7/generate_bitstream.tcl) with timing/utilization validation. Constraints file for system clock/reset/UART/LEDs. Note: requires Vivado 2024.x to synthesize -- not verifiable on macOS without Vivado.

userStories.title: MicroBlaze C firmware: Tier 1 benchmark (accelerated vs software)
userStories.description: As a firmware engineer, I need C code that loads weights into the BRAM, runs a GEMM operation via the accelerator, times it, then runs the same operation in pure software, and prints both cycle counts over UART.
acceptanceCriteria: firmware/tier1_bench.c: loads 1M hardcoded ternary weights into weight_bram via AXI, runs 100 GEMM forward passes of a 768→768 projection via accelerator, measures Xil_Time() or cycle counter before/after
Same 768→768 operation implemented in software (pure C loops over int8 activations and 2-bit packed weights) with cycle measurement
UART output format: 'ACCEL: N cycles  SW: M cycles  Speedup: K.Kx\r\n'
Speedup must be > 1.0x (accelerator faster than software on MicroBlaze at 100 MHz)
Compiles with mb-gcc -O2 -Wall without errors
userStories.notes: Created firmware/tier1_bench.c with: deterministic 1M-param weight init, accelerator forward pass (768 activations -> 768 outputs via AXI GEMM wrapper), pure-C software reference, XTime-based cycle measurement, UART output (ACCEL/SW cycles + speedup), verification step. Compiles with mb-gcc -O2 -Wall (bare-metal standalone BSP).
